ety.text: From Middle English ymage, borrowed from Old French image, from Latin imāgō (“a copy, likeness, image”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eym-; the same PIE root is the source of imitari (“to copy, imitate”); see imitate. Doublet of imago.

senses.d: A visual or other representation of the external form of something in art.
ex: The Bible forbids the worship of graven images.

senses.d: A file on a computer containing a single frame; an image file.
A mental picture of something not real or not present.
A statue or idol.
A file that contains all information needed to produce a live working copy. (See disk image and image copy.)
ex: Most game console emulators do not come with any ROM images for copyright reasons.

senses.d: A characteristic of a person, group or company etc., style, manner of dress, how one is or wishes to be perceived by others.
The value a function maps some argument to.
ex: The number 6 is the image of 3 under f that is defined as f(x) = 2x.

senses.d: The subset of the codomain of a function comprising those elements that are the image of some element of its domain.
ex: The image of this step function is the set of integers.

senses.d: A form of interference: a weaker "copy" of a strong signal that occurs at a different frequency.
Show; appearance; cast.
ex: The face of things a frightful image bears.

senses.d: To represent by an image or symbol; to portray.
ex: […] his behaviour was, as I had imaged to myself, solemnly devout.

senses.d: To reflect, mirror.
ex: Sorrow was dead indeed in her, but peace and perfect happiness were born; imaged in her tranquil beauty and profound repose.

senses.d: To create an image of.
To create a complete backup copy of a file system or other entity.

senses.d: One who leads the salat prayers in a mosque.
ex: Sheik Mohammad Seyed Tantawi, Egypt’s highest-ranking imam, led the prayers over the coffin, covered with an Egyptian flag.

senses.d: A Shi'ite Muslim leader descended from the prophet Muhammad and functioning as his spiritual successor.
One of the Twelve imams, descendants of Muhammad from the seventh to ninth centuries CE who lived exemplary lives.

From Middle English ymaginacioun, from Old French imaginacion, ymaginacion, from Latin imāginātiō. Equivalent to imagine + -ation.

senses.d: The image-making power of the mind; the act of mentally creating or reproducing an object not previously perceived; the ability to create such images.
ex: Imagination is one of the most advanced human faculties.
She removed Stranleigh’s coat with a dexterity that aroused his imagination.

senses.d: Particularly, construction of false images; fantasizing.
ex: You think someone's been following you? That's just your imagination.

senses.d: Creativity; resourcefulness.
ex: His imagination makes him a valuable team member.

senses.d: A mental image formed by the action of the imagination as a faculty; something imagined.
ex: It is a pleasant imagination to conceive a spirit iustly ballanced betweene two equall desires.

ety.text: From Middle English ymaginarie, ymagynary, from Latin imāginārius (“relating to images, fancied”), from imāgō, equivalent to imagine + -ary. The mathematical sense derives from René Descartes's use (of the French imaginaire) in 1637, La Geometrie, to ridicule the notion of regarding non-real roots of polynomials as numbers. Although Descartes' usage was derogatory, the designation stuck even after the concept gained acceptance in the 18th century.

senses.d: Existing only in the imagination.
ex: imaginary friend
Unicorns are imaginary.

senses.d: Relating or belonging to the imagination.
ex: Fiction refers to imaginary stories.

senses.d: Having no real part; that part of a complex number which is a multiple of √ (called imaginary unit).
Imagination; fancy.
An imaginary number.
The set of values, institutions, laws, and symbols common to a particular social group and the corresponding society through which people imagine their social whole.

senses.d: To form a mental image of something; to envision or create something in one's mind.
ex: Try to imagine a pink elephant.
Imagine yourself in a packed airport lounge.

senses.d: To believe in something created by one's own mind, often something false.
ex: She imagined that the man wanted to kill her.
There's nothing there; you're just imagining things.

senses.d: To assume; to suppose.
ex: I imagine that he will need to rest after such a long flight.

senses.d: To conjecture; to guess.
ex: I cannot even imagine what you are up to!
The board imagines the merger will increase profits by 25%

senses.d: To use one's imagination.
ex: Imagine that we were siblings.

senses.d: To contrive in purpose; to scheme; to devise.
ex: How long wil ye imagine miſchiefe againſt a man?

senses.d: Used to mock an idea by suggesting that it is ridiculous or ill thought through.
ex: Imagine thinking that would work.

senses.d: A short fanfic or prompt placing a reader insert in a novel scenario with a character or celebrity.
ex: If I get inspired immediately, I can bust out an imagine in 5-10 minutes.
Some imagines are more sexual and creepy than others: "Imagine Stiles walking in on you giving Scott a blowjob."

grp.label: (transitive) to form a mental image of something
